families.axis: advantage merely registered → good actively credited

members.tone: Cool, calculating approval — it rates a thing by the edge it hands you and says nothing about whether that edge is deserved or does any good.
Warmer than *advantageous*: the advantage reads as conditions tilting your way rather than as an edge coldly reckoned up.
The British spelling of *favorable*, carrying the identical tilt-in-your-favour approval with no shift in force.
Formal and firmly approving — it credits the thing with actually improving matters, where *advantageous* only counts the edge gained.
The same claim as *beneficial* stripped of its formality, asserting the benefit flatly instead of arguing for it.
Brisk and informal — it books a thing on the credit side without pausing to weigh how much good is in it.
Broad and unemphatic approval that places a thing on the good side without naming the advantage, where *beneficial* names it.
Accusatory where its neighbours approve — it treats the partiality itself as the offence rather than as a favour worth having.
Flat and administrative: it records that partiality is in play and leaves untouched the question *discriminatory* settles against it.

members.gloss: worth having or seeking or achieving
members.tone: The measured, unheated verdict — it says a thing is worth having without claiming anyone is straining after it, which is what *coveted* adds.
Loads the wanting with hunger, so the thing is not merely worth having but longed for hard, far greedier than the flat *in demand*.
States much-wantedness as a plain fact about a thing's standing, with none of the appetite audible in *coveted*.
Puts the wanting into motion — the thing is actively pursued, where *in demand* leaves it a standing condition.
The hyphen compresses that same pursuit into a single modifier that can sit in front of the noun it flatters.
Relishing rather than clinical, it savours the desire the thing arouses where *sexually attractive* merely reports it.
Flat and explicit, naming the arousal outright without a trace of the relish in *delectable*.
Praises a thing by pointing at the sourness it stirs in whoever lacks it, so the approval arrives through someone else's discontent.
Informal and relishing, it heaps the desirability higher than the sober *desirable* and sounds pleased with itself for saying so.
A comparative and nothing more — it rates one thing above another without claiming either is wanted much at all.
Settles the comparison that *preferable* is still arguing, presenting the ranking as already decided rather than urged.

families.axis: a thing handled wrongly → a person wholly cast as the victim of it

members.gloss: used incorrectly or carelessly or for an improper purpose
members.tone: The flattest of these - it faults the handling, whether careless or deliberate, without yet accusing anyone of cruelty.

members.gloss: used improperly or excessively especially drugs
members.tone: Harder than *misused* because excess joins impropriety - the fault lies in how much as well as how, drugs squarely included.
Cold and calculating beside *ill-used* - it implies someone drew profit from the person, and names the gain rather than the hurt.
Formal and plain-spoken - a verdict that a wrong was done, without *exploited*'s implication that anyone gained by it.

Informal, and the only one of these that shows the wrong from the sufferer's side - the person is imposed on and visibly feels it, where *ill-used* and *exploited* merely report what was done to them.
Bare and cutting - the unmodified participle reduces the person to an instrument, saying far less than *exploited* and landing colder for it.
The strongest of the set - it does not merely report the wrong but makes the person's whole standing consist in having suffered it.
British spelling of *victimized*, and it carries the same total verdict - the person defined by the wrong rather than merely subjected to it.

families.axis: damage named with contempt → damage merely recorded

members.tone: The family's flat baseline: harm has occurred, and the word passes no verdict on the state it left, where *dilapidated* passes little else.

members.gloss: damaged by blows or hard usage
members.tone: Puts the cause inside the word - blows and hard usage - where *damaged* leaves the cause blank.

members.gloss: damaged by blows or hard usage
members.tone: Informal where *battered* is neutral in register, treating the same hard usage as something to shrug at rather than record.

members.gloss: damaged by blows or hard usage
members.tone: The fuller form of *beat-up*, equally informal, with a little more of the beating still audible in it.
Wears the deplorable condition on the surface, making it look pitiable rather than shameful, where *derelict* makes it a reproach.
Names the deplorable state as something that has given way, plainer and more mechanical than *tatterdemalion*.
Condemning rather than descriptive - the deplorable state reads as neglect that was allowed to happen, where *dented* is only a fact about a shape.
The formal word for the deplorable state, presenting it as advanced and cumulative decay rather than the single mishap *dented* records.
Adds precariousness to the deplorable state - the thing is not merely poor but barely holding together, which *damaged* never implies.
The most ornate word in this set, and the flourish makes the contempt sound almost relished beside plain *broken-down*.
Plain-spoken where *tatterdemalion* is ornate, and it leaves the deplorable state one shove from collapse.
Damage as deformation rather than breakage: the shape has gone but not necessarily the use, which *broken* denies outright.
Deformation taken across the whole of a thing rather than along one line, so it reads as more thorough than *bent* while judging just as little.
The most local of these three - one blow's worth of deformation, where *crumpled* takes the whole surface.

members.gloss: out of working order (‘busted’ is an informal substitute for ‘broken’)
members.tone: A verdict on function alone: the thing does not work, and the word says nothing about how it got there, where *battered* says little else.

members.gloss: out of working order (‘busted’ is an informal substitute for ‘broken’)
members.tone: The informal substitute for *broken*, and the drop in register makes the same failure sound offhand rather than serious.

families.axis: sound knowledge → worldly experience so complete nothing impresses

members.gloss: having or appealing to those having worldly knowledge and refinement and savoir-faire
members.tone: Praises worldly knowledge and refinement together, and it settles on the thing made for such a person as easily as on the person - a reach *urbane* lacks.

members.gloss: very sophisticated especially because of surfeit; versed in the ways of the world
members.tone: The sophistication is charged to surfeit, which sours the praise - it marks a person as past being impressed where *worldly* only marks them as experienced.

members.gloss: very sophisticated especially because of surfeit; versed in the ways of the world
members.tone: Takes the versed-in-the-ways-of-the-world half of the sense straight, crediting the experience without the taint of excess *blase* carries.
The approval is for sound knowledge itself, with none of the social finish *sophisticated* insists on.
Flatter than *intelligent* - the credit goes to what a person knows, not to anything in the knower.

members.gloss: showing a high degree of refinement and the assurance that comes from wide social experience
members.tone: Praise for the finish, where the assurance is the visible surface and *refined* names the quality under it.

members.gloss: showing a high degree of refinement and the assurance that comes from wide social experience
members.tone: Names the refinement itself rather than its display, so it praises without the suggestion of buffing that *polished* carries.

members.gloss: showing a high degree of refinement and the assurance that comes from wide social experience
members.tone: The formal member, putting the weight on assured ease of manner rather than the surface shine *polished* names.

members.gloss: experienced in and wise to the ways of the world
members.tone: Praises shrewdness rather than polish - it says a person cannot be fooled, which *urbane* never claims.

families.axis: merely having life in one → brimming with it

members.gloss: having life or vigor or spirit
members.tone: Mild approval - credits a thing with visible vigor without claiming it brims over the way *lively* does.

members.gloss: having life or vigor or spirit
members.tone: Praise cut back to a bare condition - where *animated* shows the vigor off, this only asserts that it is there.
Flat and causal - the liveliness was put in from outside, so the word credits the doing rather than the thing.
Frankly admiring where *enlivened* stays descriptive - the same imparted liveliness heard as a virtue rather than an effect.

members.gloss: full of spirit; full of life
members.tone: A step past *animated*'s mere possession of spirit to fullness of it, and the warmth rises with the quantity.

members.gloss: full of spirit; full of life
members.tone: Elevated in register - the same fullness of life as *lively*, but weightier, sounding like a force within rather than a liveliness on show.

members.gloss: given fresh life or vigor or spirit
members.tone: States the restoration plainly - fresh vigor recorded as an outcome, with none of the relief *revived* carries.

members.gloss: given fresh life or vigor or spirit
members.tone: Warmer than *reanimated* for the same return of vigor - the fresh life sounds like a recovery worth welcoming.

families.axis: a bare warrant that something passes → rightness actively inflicted as deserts

members.tone: The bar it sets is internal and low - the thing clears your conscience rather than being right in itself, so it approves far more faintly than *fitting*.
Approval by exactness rather than permission - not merely allowable but precisely right, and it says so plainly where *meet* pronounces.
The same verdict as *fitting* delivered as a formal pronouncement, weighty and a little ceremonious, so the rightness sounds handed down rather than observed.

members.gloss: given or inflicted in requital according to merits or deserts
members.tone: Cool and measured - what it approves is the fit between deserts and what is dealt out, not whatever it lands on, and it never softens the fact that the thing is inflicted.

members.gloss: given or inflicted in requital according to merits or deserts
members.tone: Carries the same verdict as *retributive* with more machinery in the mouth, sounding like the working of paying back rather than the principle behind it.

members.gloss: given or inflicted in requital according to merits or deserts
members.tone: Points at the rightness rather than the sting - where *retributive* names the paying back, this frames the same act as a claim made good.
Approval of the coldest kind - a warrant rather than a compliment, resting on validity where *conscionable* rests on conscience.

members.gloss: having or showing or requiring special skill
members.tone: Plain, checkable praise — it credits capability without admiring it, and can sit on the work that demands the skill as easily as on the person who has it.
Praise with attainment behind it — skill brought to a high finish, warmer and more admiring than the flat *skilled*.
Approves by totality rather than dazzle — it says nothing is missing from the skill, a cooler verdict than *accomplished*.

members.gloss: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude
members.tone: Praise for deft, unlaboured sureness — it admires the aptitude in the doing where *expert* admires the knowing.

members.gloss: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude
members.tone: The authoritative member: it grants knowledge that can be leaned on and vouched for, weightier and less warm than *good*.

members.gloss: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude
members.tone: The mildest approval here — it concedes competence and stops, where *expert* confers standing.

members.gloss: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude
members.tone: Credits skill that has been worked in until it is habitual, steadier and less brilliant than *virtuoso*.

members.gloss: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude
members.tone: Measured, almost certifying approval — it reports that the standard is met, with none of the admiration in *masterful*.

members.gloss: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude
members.tone: Approves the handling itself — visible dexterity in execution, more concrete than the standing implied by *expert*.

members.gloss: having or showing knowledge and skill and aptitude
members.tone: The British spelling, carrying exactly the approving weight of *skillful* for deftness in execution.

members.gloss: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill
members.tone: Superlative praise — skill carried to its finish with nothing left to add, far above the workaday *proficient*.

members.gloss: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill
members.tone: Praise that hears authority in the skill — command of the craft, where *accomplished* only reports a high finish.

members.gloss: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill
members.tone: Admires mastery in the execution rather than in the person, the quieter of the pair beside *masterful*.

members.gloss: having or revealing supreme mastery or skill
members.tone: Praise pitched at display — mastery brilliant enough to be watched, showier than the sober *consummate*.

members.gloss: marked by great skill especially in meticulous technique
members.tone: Praise for fineness of touch — skill admired for precision and restraint rather than the power heard in *masterful*.
